en_aliases: Center for AI Standards and Innovation
definition_en: A government-backed body that evaluates frontier AI models and develops safety testing methodology. The UK and US created the first two in 2023; an International Network of AI Safety Institutes was launched at the 2024 Seoul summit. The US body was reorganised as the Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) in June 2025.
definition_zh: 由政府设立或支持、负责评测前沿人工智能模型并研究安全测试方法的专门机构。英国和美国于 2023 年率先设立，2024 年首尔峰会上成立了人工智能安全研究所国际网络。中国没有对应的监管型机构，而是在 2025 年 2 月成立了以对外交流为主的「中国人工智能发展与安全研究网络」。
pitfalls: The Chinese term is a straightforward calque, but the institutional referent does not exist in the PRC. China's nearest counterpart, 中国人工智能发展与安全研究网络 (CnAISDA, launched around the February 2025 Paris summit), is a 网络 (network) of existing institutes, not a 研究所, and does not test frontier models or hold regulatory power — so 'China's AI Safety Institute' is a misleading gloss. Note also that IDAIS's own Chinese text renders 'AI safety authorities' as 安全监管部门 (safety *regulatory* departments), a different institutional idea from a research institute. Finally, the US renaming to CAISI dropped 安全 entirely: 美国人工智能标准与创新中心 has no 安全 in it, and Chinese sources mark this by writing （原人工智能安全研究所）.

translations.notes: Standard rendering for the UK/US/Japan/Korea bodies and for the international network. Used unchanged by CAICT, 安全内参 and Chinese media.

attestations.quote_zh: 在首尔峰会上，人工智能安全研究所国际网络正式成立，标志着人工智能安全科学研究的国际合作正式启动。
attestations.quote_en: At the Seoul Summit, the International Network of AI Safety Institutes was formally established, marking the official start of international cooperation on the science of AI safety.
attestations.source_title: 从国际人工智能峰会看治理趋势变化
attestations.publisher: 安全内参（原载《中国信息安全》，作者单位中国信息通信研究院安全研究所）

attestations.quote_zh: OpenAI、Anthropic 等头部企业已经与美国人工智能标准与创新中心（原人工智能安全研究所）、英国人工智能安全研究所达成合作，允许其提前接入企业最新开发的先进模型进行测试。
attestations.quote_en: Leading firms such as OpenAI and Anthropic have reached agreements with the US Center for AI Standards and Innovation (formerly the AI Safety Institute) and the UK AI Safety Institute allowing them early access to the companies' most advanced models for testing.
attestations.source_title: 人工智能治理研究报告（2025 年）
attestations.publisher: 中国信息通信研究院（CAICT）政策与经济研究所

translations.zh: 美国人工智能标准与创新中心
translations.pinyin: Měiguó réngōng zhìnéng biāozhǔn yǔ chuàngxīn zhōngxīn
translations.literal_back: US center for AI standards and innovation
translations.notes: The post-June-2025 name of the former USAISI. CAISI is normally kept as a Latin abbreviation alongside it. Chinese coverage consistently flags the rename as a shift of remit from safety to competitiveness and national-security risk.

attestations.quote_zh: 美国商务部已将人工智能安全研究所（USAISI）正式更名为美国人工智能标准与创新中心（CAISI）
attestations.quote_en: The US Department of Commerce has formally renamed the AI Safety Institute (USAISI) as the Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI).
attestations.source_title: 【AI治理周报6月第2周】美国人工智能安全研究所现已正式改组为人工智能标准与创新中心（CAISI）
attestations.publisher: 智源社区 (BAAI Hub)

translations.zh: 中国人工智能发展与安全研究网络
translations.pinyin: Zhōngguó réngōng zhìnéng fāzhǎn yǔ ānquán yánjiū wǎngluò
translations.literal_back: China AI development and safety research network
translations.notes: Proper name of the PRC's counterpart body (abbreviated CnAISDA in English). Deliberately a 网络 spanning CAICT, Tsinghua, Shanghai AI Lab and CCID rather than a single institute, and framed as 发展与安全 (development *and* safety) rather than safety alone. Do not translate 'AI Safety Institute' into this name.

attestations.quote_zh: 中国人工智能发展与安全研究网络
attestations.quote_en: China AI Safety and Development Association / Network

Worth knowing because it shows that in a governance (as opposed to journalistic) register, the English 'AI safety institute/authority' is often reframed in Chinese as a regulator, not a research institute.

attestations.quote_zh: 各国的安全监管部门可召集会议，合作制定并承诺实施模型注册和披露制度、事故报告机制、预警触发点及应急预案。
attestations.quote_en: National AI safety authorities can convene to jointly develop and commit to implementing model registration and disclosure regimes, incident reporting mechanisms, early-warning tripwires and contingency plans.
attestations.source_title: IDAIS-Venice 共识声明（中文声明）
attestations.publisher: International Dialogues on AI Safety (IDAIS) / Safe AI Forum

used_by.note: in 《人工智能治理研究报告（2025年）》, for the UK/US bodies

used_by.note: for the International Network of AI Safety Institutes
official Chinese statement text renders 'AI safety authorities' this way

usage_examples.zh: 英国人工智能安全研究所对模型进行了部署前测试，而中国目前尚无承担同类职能的机构。
usage_examples.en: The UK AI Safety Institute ran pre-deployment testing on the model; China currently has no body performing that function.

definition_en: Rules aimed specifically at the most capable general-purpose models, usually triggered by a capability or compute threshold rather than by application sector.
definition_zh: 专门针对能力最强的通用人工智能模型的监管规则，通常以能力或算力阈值（而非应用行业）作为触发条件。
pitfalls: 前沿人工智能 is a settled term, but the *regulatory category* it names in English has no PRC counterpart. Chinese regulation is organised by 分类分级监管 (classified and graded oversight) keyed to application scenario, 智能化水平 and 应用规模 — not by a 'frontier' tier. So 前沿人工智能监管 reads to a PRC policy audience as a description of foreign (EU/UK/US) practice rather than a domestic instrument. Also note 监管 (regulation by a state organ) vs 治理 (governance, multi-stakeholder) vs 管理 (administration): choosing 监管 makes the claim that a regulator is doing it.

translations.notes: The head term is fully settled in Chinese AI-safety writing; 前沿大模型 (frontier large model) is a common variant in policy prose.

attestations.quote_zh: 上海人工智能实验室联合安远 AI，于 2025 年 7 月正式发布《前沿人工智能风险管理框架（1.0 版）》，旨在为通用型人工智能模型开发者提供全面的风险管理指导方针。
attestations.quote_en: Shanghai AI Laboratory, together with Concordia AI, formally released the Frontier AI Risk Management Framework (v1.0) in July 2025, aiming to give developers of general-purpose AI models comprehensive risk-management guidance.
attestations.source_title: 《前沿人工智能风险管理框架 2.0》
attestations.publisher: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远 AI (Concordia AI)

translations.notes: Compositional and readily understood, but not a fixed PRC policy category; I could not recover it as a set phrase in an authoritative Chinese source. Use it for describing EU/UK/US regimes.

The PRC-native alternative that occupies the same policy slot: instead of carving out a 'frontier' tier, TC260 and CAC grade all AI applications by scenario, intelligence level and deployment scale. Not a synonym — record both and say which system you are describing.

attestations.quote_zh: 推动人工智能安全相关立法，完善基础设施安全防护、分级分类监管、人工智能安全测评、最终用途管理、重点场景安全应用等制度。
attestations.quote_en: Advance legislation on AI safety, and improve systems for infrastructure security protection, graded and classified oversight, AI safety evaluation, end-use management and safe application in key scenarios.
attestations.source_title: 《人工智能安全治理框架》2.0 版
attestations.publisher: 全国网络安全标准化技术委员会 (TC260) / 国家计算机网络应急技术处理协调中心

used_by.org: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远 AI

used_by.note: the PRC's structural alternative to a frontier tier

usage_examples.zh: 欧盟以算力阈值触发前沿人工智能监管，我国则以应用场景和智能化水平进行分级分类监管。
usage_examples.en: The EU triggers frontier AI regulation via a compute threshold, whereas China grades and classifies oversight by application scenario and level of autonomy.

definition_en: Using access to AI training hardware — chips, clusters, cloud capacity — as a lever of policy: thresholds, reporting duties, export restrictions and customer verification attached to compute rather than to models.
definition_zh: 把人工智能训练所需的算力资源（芯片、集群、云服务）作为政策抓手：围绕算力设定阈值、报告义务、出口限制和客户核验，而不是直接监管模型本身。
pitfalls: 算力 is an unusually strong native term — it is standard in PRC industrial policy (东数西算, 算力网络, 算力设施) and needs no explanation. But that strength is a trap: in PRC usage 算力 policy is overwhelmingly about *building and allocating* compute as infrastructure, not about *restricting* it as a safety lever. A Chinese reader seeing 算力治理 will most likely think of scheduling, green energy and market order, not of training-run thresholds. I could not verify 算力治理 verbatim in an authoritative source, so treat the compound as unsettled and gloss it on first use.

translations.notes: Transparent, idiomatic and the obvious compound, but no verbatim occurrence in an authoritative Chinese source was recovered in the research pass or in this audit. Carried as `proposed` rather than `common` because `common` asserts repeated attested use, which we cannot evidence; this is a rendering we are putting forward, not one we have observed. Entry confidence stays low. Promote to `common` or `established` only on attestation.
The head term itself is fully established across PRC industrial policy and AI-safety writing alike. Where English says 'compute' as a mass noun, Chinese says 算力; 算力设施 is 'compute infrastructure'.

attestations.quote_zh: 针对模型算法、训练数据、算力设施、产品服务、应用场景，提出通过安全软件开发、数据质量提升、安全建设运维、测评监测加固等技术手段，提升人工智能技术及应用安全性的措施。
attestations.quote_en: For model algorithms, training data, compute infrastructure, products and services, and application scenarios, it proposes technical means — secure software development, data-quality improvement, secure build and operations, evaluation, monitoring and hardening — to raise the safety of AI technology and its applications.
attestations.source_title: 《人工智能安全治理框架》2.0 版
attestations.publisher: 全国网络安全标准化技术委员会 (TC260) / 国家计算机网络应急技术处理协调中心

attestations.quote_zh: 失控自我复制：系统未经授权自我外泄，独立获取算力与资金，创建并部署自身副本，建立持久存在并规避检测、抵抗关停。
attestations.quote_en: Uncontrolled self-replication: the system exfiltrates itself without authorisation, independently acquires compute and funds, creates and deploys copies of itself, establishes persistence, evades detection and resists shutdown.
attestations.source_title: 《前沿人工智能风险管理框架 2.0》
attestations.publisher: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远 AI (Concordia AI)

translations.notes: Used when describing the EU/US practice of triggering obligations above a FLOPs level. CAICT describes the EU GPAI Code of Practice as applying to models above a stated FLOPs figure, using 算力超过… phrasing.

usage_examples.zh: 算力治理的核心思路，是把监管抓手放在芯片和集群上，而不是直接管模型。
usage_examples.en: The core idea of compute governance is to place the regulatory lever on chips and clusters rather than directly on models.

definition_en: Restrictions on cross-border transfer of controlled items. In AI they cover advanced chips and manufacturing equipment, and — briefly, under a January 2025 US rule rescinded in May 2025 — model weights themselves.
definition_zh: 对受管制物项跨境转移的限制。在人工智能领域主要针对先进芯片和制造设备；2025 年 1 月美国商务部工业与安全局曾试图将模型权重本身纳入管制，该规则于同年 5 月被废除。
pitfalls: The term itself is a clean one-to-one match and needs no explanation. What does not carry over is the framing: in PRC official texts 出口管制 by other states is routinely characterised as 单边强制措施 (unilateral coercive measures) that 制造发展壁垒 (create development barriers). Using the term neutrally in a Chinese-language safety argument is fine, but expect the political valence to be read in. Note also 管制 (control, restrictive) vs 管理 (administration) vs 监管 (supervision) — 管制 is the strongest of the three.

translations.notes: The standard legal term, also the name of the PRC's own 《出口管制法》. Universal across policy, media and technical writing.

attestations.quote_zh: 但个别国家利用技术垄断和出口管制等单边强制措施制造发展壁垒，恶意阻断全球人工智能供应链，带来突出的芯片、软件、工具断供风险。
attestations.quote_en: However, certain countries use unilateral coercive measures such as technological monopoly and export controls to create barriers to development, maliciously cutting off the global AI supply chain and creating acute risks of chip, software and tooling cut-off.
attestations.source_title: 《人工智能安全治理框架》2.0 版
attestations.publisher: 全国网络安全标准化技术委员会 (TC260) / 国家计算机网络应急技术处理协调中心

attestations.quote_zh: 2025 年 1 月，商务部工业与安全局（BIS）首次发布规则，试图将 AI 模型权重本身纳入出口管制，但该规则在 5 月被新政府以“扼杀创新”为由废除。
attestations.quote_en: In January 2025 the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) issued a rule for the first time attempting to bring AI model weights themselves within export controls, but the rule was rescinded in May by the new administration on the grounds that it 'stifled innovation'.
attestations.source_title: 人工智能治理研究报告（2025 年）
attestations.publisher: 中国信息通信研究院（CAICT）政策与经济研究所

attestations.quote_zh: 评估模型或系统是否能提供专业知识（包括与云实验室合作、隐藏 DNA 合成订单、规避出口管制、检索并分析危险 DNA 序列等），协助相关行为主体获取制造生物威胁或生物武器所需的材料和设备。
attestations.quote_en: Assess whether the model or system can provide expertise — including working with cloud labs, concealing DNA synthesis orders, evading export controls, and retrieving and analysing dangerous DNA sequences — to help actors obtain the materials and equipment needed to make biological threats or weapons.
attestations.source_title: 《前沿人工智能风险管理框架 2.0》
attestations.publisher: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远 AI (Concordia AI)

used_by.note: in the 2.0 framework's framing of supply-chain risk

usage_examples.zh: 把模型权重纳入出口管制，在技术上比管制芯片困难得多。
usage_examples.en: Bringing model weights under export controls is technically far harder than controlling chips.

definition_en: A requirement that a model or algorithmic service be recorded with a regulator before or shortly after it goes to market. China operates the world's only large-scale live regime of this kind: 算法备案 under the 2022 algorithm-recommendation rules, extended to generative AI in 2023.
definition_zh: 要求模型或算法服务在上线前后向监管部门登记的制度。中国是目前唯一大规模实际运行此类制度的国家：依《互联网信息服务算法推荐管理规定》开展算法备案，2023 年经《生成式人工智能服务管理暂行办法》扩展至生成式人工智能服务（大模型备案）。
pitfalls: This is the single most important asymmetry in the category. 备案 is a *filing* — the provider submits materials and the regulator records them; it is not an approval and is legally weaker than 许可 (licensing). English coverage that renders 备案 as 'licensing' or 'approval' materially overstates it. Chinese practice further distinguishes 算法备案 (the algorithm/service, filed with CAC's national system), 大模型备案 (the generative model, handled through provincial CAC offices) and 登记 (registration of downstream apps that merely call an already-filed model). Meanwhile the IDAIS statements use 注册 for the arms-control-style 'registration of training runs above a threshold' — a third word for a third concept. Pick deliberately: 备案 = the existing PRC filing regime; 注册 = a proposed international registry; 登记 = a lighter recording step.

translations.notes: The operative PRC term. Article 17 of the Interim Measures ties generative AI to the algorithm-filing procedure of the algorithm-recommendation rules.

attestations.quote_zh: 提供具有舆论属性或者社会动员能力的生成式人工智能服务的，应当按照国家有关规定开展安全评估，并按照《互联网信息服务算法推荐管理规定》履行算法备案和变更、注销备案手续。
attestations.quote_en: Providers of generative AI services with public-opinion attributes or social-mobilisation capacity shall carry out a security assessment in accordance with relevant state provisions, and complete algorithm filing and the procedures for amending or cancelling that filing in accordance with the Provisions on the Administration of Algorithmic Recommendation in Internet Information Services.
attestations.source_title: 《生成式人工智能服务管理暂行办法》第十七条
attestations.publisher: 国家互联网信息办公室等七部门（中国网信网）

attestations.quote_zh: 此次专项行动有效督促了互联网企业完成算法备案，初步建立起算法安全审查框架，大部分平台借机优化了推荐内容多样性、减少同质化信息推送。
attestations.quote_en: This special campaign effectively pushed internet firms to complete algorithm filing and established an initial framework for algorithm security review; most platforms took the opportunity to improve the diversity of recommended content and reduce homogeneous information pushes.
attestations.source_title: 互联网信息服务算法治理：从专项行动迈向常态化长效化治理
attestations.publisher: 《中国信息安全》2025 年第 12 期（安全内参转载）

translations.notes: Industry shorthand for the generative-AI service filing. Distinct in practice from 算法备案 (different forms, different reviewing office) although the two are legally linked. CAICT reports the running totals.
TC260's phrasing for registering AI systems deployed in critical information infrastructure — a lighter, security-oriented registration than the CAC service filing.

attestations.quote_zh: 对在关键信息基础设施应用的人工智能系统进行登记备案，要求其具备与安全需求相匹配的安全防护能力。
attestations.quote_en: AI systems deployed in critical information infrastructure shall be recorded and filed, and are required to have security protection capabilities commensurate with their security needs.
attestations.source_title: 《人工智能安全治理框架》2.0 版
attestations.publisher: 全国网络安全标准化技术委员会 (TC260) / 国家计算机网络应急技术处理协调中心

translations.notes: Used in the Chinese IDAIS texts for the proposed international/domestic registration of models and training runs above a compute or capability threshold. Not the PRC regulatory term — do not swap it for 备案.

attestations.quote_zh: 我们应该立即对超过一定计算或能力阈值的人工智能模型和训练运行进行国内注册。
attestations.quote_en: We should immediately implement domestic registration for AI models and training runs above certain compute or capability thresholds.
attestations.source_title: IDAIS-Beijing《人工智能红线共识声明》（中文声明）
attestations.publisher: International Dialogues on AI Safety (IDAIS)

attestations.quote_zh: 各国的安全监管部门可召集会议，合作制定并承诺实施模型注册和披露制度、事故报告机制、预警触发点及应急预案。
attestations.quote_en: National AI safety authorities can convene to jointly develop and commit to implementing model registration and disclosure regimes, incident reporting mechanisms, early-warning tripwires and contingency plans.
attestations.source_title: IDAIS-Venice 共识声明（中文声明）
attestations.publisher: International Dialogues on AI Safety (IDAIS)

used_by.org: 国家互联网信息办公室 (CAC)
used_by.note: Art. 17, Interim Measures for Generative AI

used_by.zh_used: 备案制度 / 大模型备案

used_by.note: for threshold-triggered registration of models and training runs

usage_examples.zh: 备案是事后记录，不等于审批；把它译成 licensing 会高估这一制度的约束力。
usage_examples.en: Filing is an after-the-fact recording, not an approval; translating it as 'licensing' overstates how binding the regime is.

definition_en: A duty or practice of recording and escalating AI failures, near-misses and misuse cases — to the developer's own risk process, to a regulator, or to an international mechanism.
definition_zh: 对人工智能故障、险情和滥用事件进行记录并向上报告的机制，报告对象可以是开发者内部的风险管理流程、监管部门，或国际层面的协调机制。
pitfalls: Three near-synonyms are in play and they are not interchangeable. 事件 is the neutral 'event/incident' and is what the technical AI-safety literature uses (事件报告). 事故 implies an accident with actual harm — IDAIS's Chinese text uses 事故报告机制, which reads more severe. 安全事件 is the established cybersecurity term and drags in the whole 应急响应 apparatus. Also note that PRC regulation attaches incident duties to 应急预案 (contingency plans) and 应急演练 (drills) rather than to a standalone reporting obligation, so 'incident reporting' as a discrete regulatory instrument is weaker in the PRC system than in the EU AI Act.

translations.notes: The rendering used in Chinese frontier-AI risk-management writing, covering both near-misses (险情) and actual misuse.

attestations.quote_zh: 事件报告：建立跟踪实际环境中的“险情”和实际滥用案例的机制，并将其反馈至风险分析阶段。
attestations.quote_en: Incident reporting: establish mechanisms to track real-world 'near-misses' and actual misuse cases, and feed them back into the risk-analysis stage.
attestations.source_title: 《前沿人工智能风险管理框架 2.0》
attestations.publisher: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远 AI (Concordia AI)

attestations.quote_zh: 所有研发人员、管理层及参与人工智能系统开发或部署的相关人员，都应定期接受安全培训，培训内容应涵盖风险识别、负责任的开发实践以及事件报告流程。
attestations.quote_en: All R&D staff, management and personnel involved in developing or deploying AI systems should receive regular safety training covering risk identification, responsible development practices and incident-reporting procedures.
attestations.source_title: 《前沿人工智能风险管理框架 2.0》

pitfalls: 全球 and 国际 are both available and PRC official discourse strongly prefers 全球人工智能治理 — 《全球人工智能治理倡议》, 《全球人工智能治理行动计划》, 全球人工智能治理体系. 国际 tends to attach to bodies and processes (国际人工智能治理机构, 国际交流合作) rather than to the field as a whole. The choice is not stylistic: 全球 carries the inclusive, developing-country-facing framing the PRC advances, while 国际 reads as inter-state. Separately, 治理 (governance) is deliberately broader than 监管 (regulation) and is preferred in international texts precisely because it does not imply a supranational regulator.

definition_en: China's flagship AI governance document, announced by Xi Jinping at the Third Belt and Road Forum and released on 18 October 2023. It sets out PRC positions on development, security and governance, including risk-tiered testing and evaluation, agile governance, and support for discussing an international AI governance body under the UN.

pitfalls: Chinese is the source language here; the English title is the official translation, not the original. Cite the Chinese text. Note that 倡议 is an *initiative/proposal* — a political statement of position, not a binding instrument, and not the same speech act as a 法规, 办法 or 标准. Its key phrases are load-bearing PRC formulations that resist literal translation: 以人为本 (people-centred), 智能向善 (AI for good), 敏捷治理 (agile governance), 分类分级管理 (classified and graded management). Note also that 安全 in this document spans safety, security and national security without distinction.

definition_en: TC260's non-binding technical document setting out China's AI risk taxonomy and countermeasures. Version 1.0 was released 9 September 2024; version 2.0 on 15 September 2025, adding a three-way risk taxonomy (technology-inherent, technology-application, application-derived) and a five-level risk grading scale.
definition_zh: 全国网络安全标准化技术委员会发布的技术文件，系统提出中国的人工智能安全风险分类与应对措施。1.0 版于 2024 年 9 月 9 日发布，2.0 版于 2025 年 9 月 15 日发布，新增技术内生、技术应用、应用衍生三类风险划分，并探索五级风险分级。
pitfalls: Chinese-origin document — cite the Chinese. The 2.0 PDF is bilingual on its title page and gives its own English title as 'AI Safety Governance Framework 2.0', so 安全 here is officially rendered *safety*; be aware that secondary English commentary sometimes renders it 'AI Security Governance Framework', and the document's contents in fact cover security (漏洞, 后门, 供应链) as much as safety. It is a 技术文件, not a 国家标准 — it is not mandatory and carries no penalties, so calling it 'China's AI safety standard' overstates it. Note also that 治理 (governance) not 监管 (regulation) is in the title, consistent with its non-binding status.

translations.notes: Official title. The document's own title page carries the English 'AI Safety Governance Framework 2.0', making this one of the strongest attested EN↔ZH pairs in the whole category.

definition_en: The European Union's horizontal AI regulation, structured around risk tiers, with separate obligations for general-purpose AI models. Its implementation phase — harmonised standards, regulatory sandboxes, and a November 2025 simplification proposal — is now the main subject of Chinese commentary.
definition_zh: 欧盟以风险分级为核心的人工智能横向立法，并对通用人工智能模型设有单独义务。中文评论目前主要关注其落地阶段：协调标准制定、监管沙盒试点，以及 2025 年 11 月欧盟委员会提出的简化修订提案。
pitfalls: The rendering is genuinely unsettled between 《人工智能法案》 and 《人工智能法》 — CAICT's 2025 governance report uses both within the same document. 法案 strictly means 'bill' (a draft before enactment), so now that the Act is in force 《人工智能法》 is the more accurate word, yet 法案 remains the more widely circulated form. Either is understood; 《欧盟人工智能法案》 is the safer choice for recognisability, 《欧盟人工智能法》 the more precise. Also note that Chinese sources often discuss the associated 《通用型人工智能模型行为准则》 (GPAI Code of Practice) as a separate instrument.

translations.notes: Most widely circulated form. Competes with 《欧盟人工智能法》; the choice signals whether the writer treats it as a bill or as enacted law.
Used in the same CAICT report when citing specific articles, which suggests it is becoming the preferred form for legal-technical reference now that the Regulation is in force.

attestations.quote_en: Article 5 of the EU AI Act expressly prohibits AI systems that cause physical or psychological harm to humans, and Article 50 requires high-risk AI systems with affective-interaction functions to provide detailed technical documentation, transparency reports and comprehensive risk-assessment evidence.

pitfalls: The renaming is the whole story and the Chinese tracks it faithfully: 安全 was in the first summit's name and has been absent from every subsequent one — 人工智能首尔峰会, 巴黎人工智能行动峰会, and the 2026 Indian edition. So 人工智能安全峰会 is correct only for Bletchley and as a name for the series' original character; using it as a generic label for the series implies a safety focus that the later meetings dropped. Chinese sources normally carry the English name in parentheses on first mention, which is a good habit to copy.

definition_en: A track-two dialogue series convening senior AI scientists from China and the West, organised by the Safe AI Forum. Meetings: Oxford (2023), Beijing (March 2024), Venice (September 2024), Shanghai (July 2025), London (April 2026). Each issues a consensus statement in parallel English and Chinese.
definition_zh: 由 Safe AI Forum 组织的二轨对话系列，汇集中西方资深人工智能科学家，已举办牛津（2023）、北京（2024 年 3 月）、威尼斯（2024 年 9 月）、上海（2025 年 7 月）、伦敦（2026 年 4 月）等届，每届发布中英文对照的共识声明。

pitfalls: The name is not stable in Chinese. Safe AI Forum's own Chinese page uses 人工智能安全国际对话（IDAIS）; Tsinghua AIR and Chinese media covering the Beijing meeting used 北京AI安全国际对话; and 国际人工智能安全对话 also circulates. Word order matters: 人工智能安全国际对话 = 'international dialogue on AI safety' (the English), whereas 国际人工智能安全对话 parses as 'dialogue on international AI safety'. Prefer the first. The Beijing statement's own Chinese title is 《北京AI安全国际共识》 / 《人工智能红线共识声明》, not a translation of 'IDAIS'. The bilingual statements are the single highest-value attestation source in this category — quote them directly.

definition_en: A regime in which an activity is prohibited unless a regulator has granted permission in advance. Proposed for frontier AI training and deployment; not the instrument China actually uses for AI.
definition_zh: 未经监管部门事先批准即不得从事某项活动的制度。国际上有人主张对前沿人工智能的训练和部署实行许可制，但中国目前对人工智能采用的并非许可制。
pitfalls: The essential point in this category. Chinese administrative law distinguishes 行政许可 (administrative licensing — prohibited unless permitted, governed by the 行政许可法) from 备案 (filing — permitted, but you must record it). China's AI regime is built on 备案, not 许可. English writing that calls China's algorithm/model filing a 'licensing regime' overstates the state's gatekeeping power; conversely, Chinese writing that renders proposals for frontier-AI 'licensing' as 备案 understates them. Keep the pair distinct: 许可 = licence/permission, 备案 = filing. 牌照 is the informal industry word for a licence-as-asset (telecom, finance) and carries a market-access connotation; 审批 (approval) is a third adjacent term. CAICT's report is explicit that traditional 物理准入许可 tools are failing for AI.

translations.notes: The legal term (行政许可 for the administrative-law concept, 出口许可 for export licences). Established generally; what is unattested is any PRC AI-specific licensing regime, because none exists.

attestations.quote_zh: 虽然研发能力集中在少数国家与科技巨头手中，但应用端却通过开源模型、云端处理等体现出低门槛、去中心化等特点，使得传统依赖物理准入许可、实体边界检查和静态合规审查的监管工具失效。
attestations.quote_en: Although R&D capability is concentrated in a few countries and tech giants, the application layer — via open-weight models and cloud processing — is low-barrier and decentralised, which renders ineffective the traditional regulatory toolkit of physical entry licensing, physical border checks and static compliance review.
attestations.source_title: 人工智能治理研究报告（2025 年）
attestations.publisher: 中国信息通信研究院（CAICT）政策与经济研究所

attestations.quote_zh: 与此同时，国会中出现了以国家安全为由加强管制的呼声，多项法案如《美中人工智能能力脱钩法案》《AI 监督法案》等均赋予国会直接否决相关出口许可的权力。
attestations.quote_en: At the same time, calls have emerged in Congress to tighten controls on national-security grounds, with bills such as the Decoupling America's Artificial Intelligence Capabilities from China Act and the AI Oversight Act giving Congress power to directly veto relevant export licences.
attestations.source_title: 人工智能治理研究报告（2025 年）
attestations.publisher: 中国信息通信研究院（CAICT）政策与经济研究所

translations.notes: Recorded here as a translation to avoid, not to use. 备案 is what China actually operates and is systematically weaker than licensing: no prior approval, no discretionary refusal in the ordinary case. Translating 'licensing' as 备案 (or 备案 as 'licensing') is the most consequential false friend in this category. See the model-registration entry.

translations.notes: Industry register, connoting a scarce market-access permit (as in telecoms or payments). Idiomatic for 'you need a licence to operate', but wrong for the administrative-law sense; use 许可 in legal or policy prose. No AI-specific attestation recovered.

usage_examples.en: China operates a filing system, not a licensing system: firms submit materials for the record rather than applying for prior approval.

definition_en: Verifying who a customer is before granting service. In AI governance it is proposed for cloud compute providers, so that large training runs cannot be bought anonymously.
definition_zh: 在提供服务前核实客户身份的制度。在人工智能治理中，主要提议用于云算力服务商，使大规模训练无法匿名购买。
pitfalls: Three separate problems. (1) Chinese practitioners usually just write KYC in Latin letters; 了解你的客户 / 认识你的客户 are glosses, and 认识你的客戶 is the Taiwan/HK form. (2) I could not verify any Chinese-language source applying KYC to AI compute providers, so the AI-governance sense appears not to have entered Chinese discourse at all — a genuine gap. (3) 实名制 / 真实身份信息认证 is a real and heavily enforced PRC regime that partly overlaps KYC but is not the same thing: it verifies the *end user* of an internet service against a national ID or mobile number, it exists for content-attribution and public-security reasons rather than anti-money-laundering, and it has never been applied to compute purchasing. Do not use 实名制 to translate KYC in a compute-governance argument; explain the difference instead.

translations.notes: The usual form in Chinese finance and compliance writing; kept in Latin letters mid-sentence. Recorded without attestation because the sources seen were not fetched in full during this pass.
The standard mainland gloss, normally written alongside the abbreviation as 了解你的客户（KYC）. No attestation recovered in an AI-governance context; treat as unverified for this field.

The PRC-native adjacent regime, imposed on deep-synthesis service providers with respect to their *users*. Legally grounded and actively enforced, but aimed at attributability of generated content, not at gating access to compute. Colloquially 实名制 (real-name system).

attestations.quote_zh: 对使用者进行真实身份信息认证
attestations.quote_en: Conduct authentication of users' true identity information.
attestations.source_title: 《互联网信息服务深度合成管理规定》

usage_examples.en: KYC for compute providers is not the same thing as China's existing real-name system for users: the former constrains the organisation buying compute, the latter the individual using a service.

definition_en: Protecting the trained parameters of a frontier model from theft or unauthorised copying, since possession of the weights confers the model's full capability without any of its deployment safeguards. RAND's SL1–SL5 scale is the reference security-level framework.
definition_zh: 防止前沿模型的训练参数被窃取或未经授权复制。一旦获得权重，攻击者即可绕过所有部署侧防护措施，完整获得模型能力。兰德公司提出的 SL1–SL5 安全等级是常见参照框架。
pitfalls: 模型权重 is fully settled, so the compound is transparent — but 安全 again collapses safety and security, and here the intended sense is unambiguously *security*. Consider 模型权重防护 or 模型权重安全防护 when the distinction matters. The bigger issue is that Chinese frontier-AI practice reaches for a different reference framework: rather than RAND's SL1–SL5, Chinese guidance maps weight protection onto 网络安全等级保护 (MLPS), requiring at least 三级（监督保护级）for models past a risk threshold. The two scales are not comparable and should never be equated — MLPS grades a whole information system's protection obligations under PRC law, while SL1–SL5 grades resistance to specified attacker capability tiers.

translations.notes: Universal in Chinese ML and policy writing; also 开放权重模型 for 'open-weight model'.

attestations.quote_zh: 2025 年 1 月，商务部工业与安全局（BIS）首次发布规则，试图将 AI 模型权重本身纳入出口管制。
attestations.quote_en: In January 2025 the Bureau of Industry and Security issued a rule for the first time attempting to bring AI model weights themselves within export controls.
attestations.source_title: 人工智能治理研究报告（2025 年）
attestations.publisher: 中国信息通信研究院（CAICT）政策与经济研究所

attestations.quote_zh: 自主潜逃：能识别并利用托管基础设施中的零日漏洞，或通过操纵管理员将模型权重导出到外部服务器。
attestations.quote_en: Autonomous escape: able to identify and exploit zero-day vulnerabilities in hosting infrastructure, or to manipulate administrators into exporting model weights to an external server.
attestations.source_title: 《前沿人工智能风险管理框架 2.0》
attestations.publisher: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远 AI (Concordia AI)

translations.notes: Compositional and immediately understood, but Chinese sources tend to express the idea through concrete measures (隔离存储、访问控制、等级保护) rather than as a named category. No verbatim occurrence of the compound recovered in this pass.

translations.zh: 模型权重采用极端隔离存储策略
translations.pinyin: móxíng quánzhòng cǎiyòng jíduān gélí cúnchǔ cèlüè
translations.literal_back: model weights use an extreme isolated-storage policy
translations.notes: How the Chinese frontier framework actually phrases the requirement — as a control, not a term. Useful as a model sentence when writing about weight security in Chinese.

attestations.quote_zh: 实施最高级别访问控制，仅限可信人员/机构访问，严禁对外暴露敏感模型；模型权重采用极端隔离存储策略，使暴露风险最小化；执行全生命周期安全审计与对抗演练；遵循等级保护标准要求。
attestations.quote_en: Apply the highest level of access control, restricted to trusted personnel and institutions, with sensitive models strictly not exposed externally; store model weights under an extreme isolation policy to minimise exposure risk; conduct full-lifecycle security audits and adversarial exercises; and comply with graded-protection standard requirements.
attestations.source_title: 《前沿人工智能风险管理框架 2.0》
attestations.publisher: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远 AI (Concordia AI)

attestations.quote_zh: 模型权重采用极端隔离存储策略，使暴露风险最小化。
attestations.quote_en: Model weights shall use an extreme isolation storage strategy so as to minimise exposure risk.
attestations.source_title: 《前沿人工智能风险管理框架 2.0》
attestations.publisher: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远 AI (Concordia AI)

used_by.org: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远 AI
used_by.zh_used: 模型权重 + 等级保护
used_by.note: maps weight protection onto China's MLPS levels rather than RAND SL tiers

usage_examples.zh: 越过红线的模型，其权重至少应按三级等级保护要求隔离存储。
usage_examples.en: For models that have crossed a red line, weights should be stored in isolation to at least MLPS Level 3 requirements.

definition_en: Risk originating from someone with legitimate access — an employee, contractor or partner — who exfiltrates weights, disables safeguards or subverts controls.
definition_zh: 由拥有合法访问权限的人员（员工、承包商、合作方）带来的风险，例如外泄模型权重、关闭防护措施或规避管控。
pitfalls: 内部威胁 is the standard security-industry calque, but in the leading Chinese frontier-AI risk framework the same two characters mean something entirely different: there, 威胁源 is split into 外部威胁 (malicious actors, terrorists), 内部威胁 — glossed explicitly as 模型自身的未对齐或欺骗倾向, i.e. the model itself — and 情境性威胁 (human operator error). So in Chinese AI-safety writing 内部威胁 can denote *the AI* rather than a rogue human. This is a real and easily-missed false friend. If you mean a malicious employee, disambiguate: 内部人员威胁 or 内部人员风险. The colloquial 内鬼 ('inside ghost', a mole) is vivid and widely understood but too informal for policy prose, and no attestation for it was recovered in an AI context.

translations.notes: Standard in cybersecurity for the malicious-insider sense, but redefined in Chinese frontier-AI risk writing to mean the model's own misalignment. Always check which sense a source intends.

attestations.quote_zh: 威胁源（T）：危害的发起方，可分为外部威胁（如恶意行为者、恐怖分子）、内部威胁（如模型自身的未对齐或欺骗倾向）以及情境性威胁（如人为操作失误）。
attestations.quote_en: Threat source (T): the originator of harm, divided into external threats (e.g. malicious actors, terrorists), internal threats (e.g. the model's own misalignment or deceptive tendencies), and situational threats (e.g. human operating error).
attestations.source_title: 《前沿人工智能风险管理框架 2.0》
attestations.publisher: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远 AI (Concordia AI)

translations.notes: We recommend this when the human sense is meant, precisely because 内部威胁 has been claimed for the misaligned-model sense in Chinese frontier-AI writing. Adding 人员 costs two characters and removes the ambiguity entirely. Not attested; this is our coinage for disambiguation.
Colloquial and vivid, common in Chinese reporting on data-leak cases. Too informal for standards or policy text, and no AI-specific attestation was recovered.
How TC260 expresses the countermeasure side without naming the threat category — via least-privilege access control rather than a named 'insider threat' programme.

attestations.quote_zh: 严格管理人工智能应用权限，通过最小权限原则等手段强化内部安全管理，增强账户安全性，在处理敏感数据时使用加密技术等保护措施。
attestations.quote_en: Strictly manage AI application permissions; strengthen internal security management through means such as the principle of least privilege; enhance account security; and use protective measures such as encryption when handling sensitive data.
attestations.source_title: 《人工智能安全治理框架》2.0 版
attestations.publisher: 全国网络安全标准化技术委员会 (TC260) / 国家计算机网络应急技术处理协调中心

used_by.org: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远 AI
used_by.note: used for the model's own misalignment, not for rogue staff

usage_examples.zh: 这里说的“内部威胁”指的是内部人员，而不是模型自身的未对齐倾向。
usage_examples.en: 'Insider threat' here means human insiders, not the model's own misalignment.

definition_en: A halt on developing or deploying systems above some capability level, whether self-imposed by a developer, agreed across an industry, or mandated. The FLI open letter of March 2023 calling for a six-month pause is the canonical instance.
definition_zh: 对超过一定能力水平的系统停止开发或部署，可以是开发者自我约束、行业共同约定或由监管强制。最有代表性的是 2023 年 3 月生命未来研究所发起的呼吁暂停六个月的公开信。
pitfalls: 暂停 (suspend, temporarily) is the natural and attested word, but it is weaker than English 'moratorium', which implies a formal, agreed, bounded halt. 禁令 (ban/injunction) is far stronger and implies legal prohibition — do not use it for a voluntary pause. 停止 is permanent-sounding. The Chinese-language conversation around the 2023 pause letter was largely framed as 呼吁暂停训练 rather than as a governance instrument, and the idea has little purchase in PRC policy discourse, where the framing is 统筹发展和安全 (coordinating development and security) — i.e. that development should not stop. Expect a Chinese reader to hear 暂停 as an operational control rather than a policy demand.

translations.notes: Attested in Chinese frontier-AI risk work as an operational decision: the red zone of the risk framework is defined as 暂停部署或开发. This is the strongest, most concrete Chinese usage of the concept.

attestations.quote_zh: 三类风险区分别为：绿区（常规部署、广泛可接受）、黄区（受控部署、严格管控下可容忍）或红区（暂停部署或开发、不可接受）。
attestations.quote_en: The three risk zones are: green (routine deployment, broadly acceptable), yellow (controlled deployment, tolerable under strict controls), and red (suspend deployment or development, unacceptable).
attestations.source_title: 《前沿人工智能风险管理框架 2.0》
attestations.publisher: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远 AI (Concordia AI)

attestations.quote_zh: 立即采取措施，阻断潜在灾难性后果的发生路径；执行最高级别的管控措施和操作限制；暂停相关运行或部署，直至风险降至红线以下；在恢复运营前，完成并通过独立第三方安全审查。
attestations.quote_en: Immediately act to cut off the pathway to potentially catastrophic consequences; apply the highest level of controls and operating restrictions; suspend the relevant operation or deployment until risk falls below the red line; and complete and pass an independent third-party safety review before resuming operations.
attestations.source_title: 《前沿人工智能风险管理框架 2.0》
attestations.publisher: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远 AI (Concordia AI)

translations.notes: The collocation Chinese media used for the March 2023 FLI open letter, generally reported as 呼吁暂停训练比 GPT-4 更强大的 AI 系统. Recorded without attestation — the sources seen for it were search listings rather than pages fetched in full during this pass.
Recommended against as a rendering of 'moratorium'. 禁令 implies a legally binding prohibition with penalties, which overstates every real proposal in this space. Reserve it for actual bans.

used_by.org: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远 AI
used_by.note: definition of the red risk zone

usage_examples.zh: 风险一旦进入红区，应暂停部署或开发，直至风险降至红线以下。
usage_examples.en: Once risk enters the red zone, deployment or development should be suspended until risk falls below the red line.

definition_en: Establishing, to the satisfaction of a party that does not trust you, that a claim about an AI system or about your compliance with an agreement is true. Spans technical verification of model properties and arms-control-style mutual verification between states.
definition_zh: 在互不信任的前提下，使他方确信关于人工智能系统的某项主张或对协议的遵守情况属实。既包括对模型性质的技术性验证，也包括国家间军控式的相互核查。
pitfalls: Chinese splits what English fuses, and the split is worth preserving. 验证 is technical validation — you check that a property holds (可被技术验证, 实证验证, 沙箱验证). 核查 is inspection of another party's claims, the word used in arms control and in audit (核查开发者的主张, 核查合规情况); 核实 is its near-synonym for confirming a fact. Using 验证 where you mean adversarial inter-state inspection loses the whole point; using 核查 for a technical property sounds like an audit. The IDAIS Chinese statements use both within one passage and are the best model. Note also 可验证的 for 'verifiable' in the IDAIS-Shanghai red-lines formulation 可验证的全球性行为红线.

translations.notes: The arms-control and audit sense. This is the word to use for verified compliance between distrustful parties.

attestations.quote_zh: 定期内部审计：定期开展内部审计，核查人工智能安全方案的合规情况，并及时发现现有安全措施中的薄弱环节。
attestations.quote_en: Regular internal audit: conduct internal audits periodically to check compliance with the AI safety plan and identify weaknesses in existing safeguards in good time.
attestations.source_title: 《前沿人工智能风险管理框架 2.0》
attestations.publisher: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远 AI (Concordia AI)

translations.notes: The technical sense: establishing that a property of a system holds, through testing, simulation or formal means. TC260 makes 可客观验证 one of its governance goals.

attestations.quote_zh: 促进可客观验证：研究构建客观、公正、透明的测试与认证机制，推动人工智能系统的功能、性能、安全特性、决策链条等方面可被技术验证。
attestations.quote_en: Promote objective verifiability: research and build objective, impartial and transparent testing and certification mechanisms so that AI systems' functionality, performance, safety properties and decision chains can be technically verified.
attestations.source_title: 《人工智能安全治理框架》2.0 版
attestations.publisher: 全国网络安全标准化技术委员会 (TC260) / 国家计算机网络应急技术处理协调中心

attestations.quote_zh: 制定明确的测试规则和方法，包括人工测试、自动测试、混合测试等，利用沙箱仿真等技术对模型进行充分测试和验证。
attestations.quote_en: Set clear testing rules and methods — manual, automated and hybrid testing — and use techniques such as sandbox simulation to thoroughly test and verify models.
attestations.source_title: 《人工智能安全治理框架》2.0 版
attestations.publisher: 全国网络安全标准化技术委员会 (TC260) / 国家计算机网络应急技术处理协调中心

translations.notes: Used in the IDAIS-Shanghai formulation 可验证的全球性行为红线, whose parallel English is 'verifiable global behavioural red lines' — a directly attested translation pair.

attestations.quote_zh: 通过加强国际协调，共同确立并恪守可验证的全球性行为红线。
attestations.quote_en: Through stronger international coordination, jointly establish and abide by verifiable global behavioural red lines.
attestations.source_title: IDAIS-Shanghai 共识声明（中文声明）
attestations.publisher: International Dialogues on AI Safety (IDAIS)

used_by.note: official Chinese statement text, parallel to 'verify' and 'verifiable'

used_by.zh_used: 可客观验证 / 技术验证

used_by.org: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远 AI

usage_examples.zh: 技术上可以验证模型的某项性质，但要让别国相信你确实这么做了，需要的是核查机制。
usage_examples.en: You can technically verify a property of a model, but convincing another state that you actually did so requires an inspection mechanism.

definition_en: A published technical specification governing how AI systems must be built, tested or protected. In China these are GB (mandatory) or GB/T (recommended) national standards, supplemented by sectoral standards and by non-binding technical documents such as the AI Safety Governance Framework.
definition_zh: 规定人工智能系统研发、测试或防护要求的技术规范。在中国分为强制性国家标准（GB）与推荐性国家标准（GB/T），并由行业标准和《人工智能安全治理框架》等不具强制力的技术文件补充。
pitfalls: The term is easy; the institutional layer beneath it is where translation goes wrong. GB = 强制性国家标准 (mandatory); GB/T = 推荐性国家标准 (recommended) — most PRC AI standards are GB/T, so calling them 'mandatory Chinese standards' is wrong, though a GB/T can become binding indirectly when a regulation or contract references it. Below national standards sit 行业标准 and 团体标准; above and beside them sit 技术文件 like TC260's framework, which are not standards at all. Note also that Chinese practice says 分类分级 for what English calls risk tiering, and that a GB/T reference number (e.g. GB/T 25070-2019) is the normal way to cite precisely — carry the number across when translating.

translations.notes: The general term. As everywhere in this category, 安全 does not disambiguate safety from security; the standard's number and scope do.

attestations.quote_zh: 遵循国家与行业安全标准：遵循《信息安全技术 网络安全等级保护安全设计技术要求》（GB/T 25070-2019）等网络安全保护国家标准，并从系统定级、系统备案、系统安全建设、系统等级测评、监督检查等五个阶段实施等级保护。
attestations.quote_en: Follow national and sectoral security standards: comply with national cybersecurity protection standards such as GB/T 25070-2019 (Information security technology — Technical requirements of security design for classified protection of cybersecurity), and implement graded protection across five stages — system grading, system filing, system security construction, system grading evaluation, and supervision and inspection.
attestations.source_title: 《前沿人工智能风险管理框架 2.0》
attestations.publisher: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远 AI (Concordia AI)

translations.notes: The GB/GB-T layer. TC260 explicitly casts national standards as the reference that sectoral regulators localise.

attestations.quote_zh: 行业领域主管（监管）部门参照国家标准制定行业标准规范、实施细则，并推动本行业领域人工智能安全应用相关分类分级工作。
attestations.quote_en: Sectoral competent (regulatory) departments shall draw on national standards to formulate sectoral standards, norms and implementing rules, and advance classification and grading work for safe AI application in their sector.
attestations.source_title: 《人工智能安全治理框架》2.0 版
attestations.publisher: 全国网络安全标准化技术委员会 (TC260) / 国家计算机网络应急技术处理协调中心

attestations.quote_zh: 推动人工智能应用安全分类分级国家标准制定工作。行业领域主管（监管）部门参照国家标准制定行业标准规范、实施细则，并推动本行业领域人工智能安全应用相关分类分级工作。
attestations.quote_en: Advance the drafting of a national standard for the security classification and grading of AI applications. Sectoral competent (regulatory) authorities shall formulate sectoral standards, specifications and implementing rules by reference to the national standard, and promote classification and grading work related to the secure application of AI in their own sector.
attestations.source_title: 《人工智能安全治理框架》2.0 版
attestations.publisher: 全国网络安全标准化技术委员会 (TC260) / 国家计算机网络应急技术处理协调中心

translations.notes: The cover-all phrase used when a text does not want to commit to a legal instrument type. Appears in the Global AI Governance Initiative's call for 具有广泛共识的人工智能治理框架和标准规范.

attestations.quote_zh: 各国应在人工智能治理中加强信息交流和技术合作，共同做好风险防范，形成具有广泛共识的人工智能治理框架和标准规范
attestations.quote_en: Countries should strengthen information exchange and technological cooperation in AI governance, jointly guard against risks, and form AI governance frameworks, standards and norms based on broad consensus.
attestations.source_title: 《全球人工智能治理倡议》
attestations.publisher: 中华人民共和国外交部

used_by.zh_used: 国家标准 / 标准规范

used_by.org: 上海人工智能实验室 / 安远 AI

usage_examples.zh: 多数人工智能安全国家标准是推荐性（GB/T），并非强制执行，但被法规或合同引用后即产生约束力。
usage_examples.en: Most AI safety national standards are recommended (GB/T) rather than mandatory, but become binding once referenced by a regulation or contract.

definition_en: Regulation of algorithmic systems — recommendation, ranking, scheduling and generation — as such. China has the most developed regime of this kind, combining the 2022 algorithm-recommendation provisions, a national filing system, periodic 清朗 enforcement campaigns and platform disclosure duties.
definition_zh: 针对推荐、排序、调度、生成等算法系统本身的治理。中国在这方面制度最为完备，结合了 2022 年《互联网信息服务算法推荐管理规定》、全国统一的算法备案系统、“清朗”专项行动以及平台公开算法规则的要求。
pitfalls: This is a case where the Chinese concept is richer than the English one, not poorer. 算法治理 in PRC usage bundles filing, campaign enforcement, platform self-disclosure, court practice and public participation into a single multi-layer regime, and has an explicit normative direction — 算法向上向善 (algorithms oriented upward and toward good) — with no English counterpart. English 'algorithmic governance' is a broader academic term that often includes governance *by* algorithms; 算法治理 in PRC usage means governance *of* algorithms. If you mean the former, say 算法化治理 or paraphrase. Note also that the substantive concerns are distinctively Chinese: 信息茧房 (information cocoons), 大数据杀熟 (price discrimination against loyal customers), and effects on gig workers. Finally, do not treat 算法备案 as an alternative rendering of this headword: filing is one instrument created within the 算法治理 regime — see the algorithm-filing entry.

translations.notes: Fully institutionalised term, used by the regulator itself.

attestations.quote_zh: 算法治理是一项长期性、系统性工程，网信部门将开展常态化巡查，督导信息推荐算法平台持续优化算法运行机制和管理规则。
attestations.quote_en: Algorithm governance is a long-term, systematic undertaking; cyberspace administration departments will conduct routine inspections and supervise information-recommendation algorithm platforms in continuously optimising algorithmic operating mechanisms and management rules.
attestations.source_title: 中央网信办持续加强信息推荐算法治理
attestations.publisher: 中央网络安全和信息化委员会办公室（中国网信网）

attestations.quote_zh: 相关法律法规为算法治理工作的开展提供了坚实的上位法依据。
attestations.quote_en: The relevant laws and regulations provide a solid statutory basis on which algorithmic governance work is carried out.
attestations.source_title: 互联网信息服务算法治理：从专项行动迈向常态化长效化治理

en_aliases: Interim Measures for the Management of Generative AI Services
definition_en: China's operative generative-AI regulation, adopted by the CAC with six other ministries and in force from 15 August 2023. It establishes security assessment, algorithm filing and complaint mechanisms, allocates provider responsibilities, and applies to services offered to the public in mainland China.
definition_zh: 中国生成式人工智能的主要规章，由国家互联网信息办公室会同六部门公布，自 2023 年 8 月 15 日起施行。规定了安全评估、算法备案、投诉举报等制度，明确提供者责任，适用于向境内公众提供生成式人工智能服务的行为。
preferred_zh: 《生成式人工智能服务管理暂行办法》
pitfalls: Chinese-origin instrument — cite the Chinese text. Every word of the title does work: 暂行 (interim/provisional) signals that a fuller instrument is expected; 办法 is a departmental rule (部门规章), which sits below a 法律 (law) and 行政法规 (administrative regulation) in the PRC hierarchy — so 'Measures' is right and 'Act' or 'Law' would be wrong; 管理 is administration, deliberately softer than 监管. And 服务 matters: the Measures regulate *services offered to the public*, not model development as such, which is why research and internal use fall outside them. Note that the substantive obligations run through cross-references to other instruments (the algorithm-recommendation provisions, the security-assessment regime), so the Measures read thinner than they operate.

definition_en: In the PRC a statutorily defined category. Article 2 of the 2015 National Security Law defines 国家安全 as the state of relative freedom from danger and from internal or external threat to state power, sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity, the people's welfare, sustainable economic and social development and other major national interests — together with the capacity to keep that state secure. The law and the 总体国家安全观 (holistic approach to national security) built on it span political, territorial, military, economic, cultural, social, technological, cyber, ecological, nuclear and further domains. The 2015 law itself does not name artificial intelligence; AI enters the category through the doctrine's later enumerations and through planning documents such as the 2025 Fourth Plenum recommendations, which call for building national security capability in emerging fields including AI.
definition_zh: 在中国，国家安全是有法律定义的范畴。《国家安全法》第二条规定，国家安全是指国家政权、主权、统一和领土完整、人民福祉、经济社会可持续发展和国家其他重大利益相对处于没有危险和不受内外威胁的状态，以及保障持续安全状态的能力。该法与在其基础上展开的“总体国家安全观”涵盖政治、国土、军事、经济、文化、社会、科技、网络、生态、核等诸多领域。2015 年法律文本本身并未出现“人工智能”；人工智能是通过总体国家安全观后续的领域列举，以及二十届四中全会建议等规划文件中“加强人工智能等新兴领域国家安全能力建设”的表述进入这一范畴的。
pitfalls: Lexically trivial, politically the most load-bearing term in the category. Three consequences for anyone writing AI-safety arguments in Chinese. (1) 国家安全 in the PRC is a defined legal category with a doctrine (总体国家安全观) and a dedicated legal apparatus; invoking it is not rhetorical framing as it often is in English, it is a jurisdictional claim that pulls a topic into a specific institutional track. (2) It is expressly one of the graded factors in TC260's risk-grading scale, alongside 社会稳定 and 公民权益 — so 'national security risk' has a defined place in Chinese AI risk taxonomy that it lacks in most Western ones. (3) Framing catastrophic-risk arguments as 国家安全 raises their salience but can also make them non-public and non-debatable. Note the systematic pairing with 发展: 统筹发展和安全 and 坚持发展和安全并重 are the standard formulations, and any argument that reads as anti-development will be discounted.

translations.notes: One-to-one lexically. What does not transfer is the legal-doctrinal weight; gloss it when the PRC-specific sense matters.

definition_en: The PRC's structural device for calibrating AI oversight: 分类 sorts risks into kinds, 分级 sorts them into severity levels. TC260's 2.0 framework classifies risks as technology-inherent, technology-application and application-derived, and grades them by severity — from 低安全风险 (low) through 一般安全风险 (general) and upward — using application scenario, level of intelligence and deployment scale, with the grading principles set out in an annex for sectors to localise.
definition_zh: 中国用于调节人工智能监管强度的制度装置：分类是按风险种类划分，分级是按严重程度划分。《人工智能安全治理框架》2.0 版将风险分为技术内生、技术应用、应用衍生三类，并以应用场景、智能化水平、应用规模为要素，按低安全风险、一般安全风险等由低到高的顺序对风险进行分级，分级原则见附件，供行业细化。
pitfalls: English collapses this into 'risk tiering' or 'risk-based regulation' and loses the two-axis structure that PRC texts insist on: 分类 (by kind) and 分级 (by severity) are separate operations and are often carried out by different bodies — national standards set the method, sectoral regulators instantiate it. It is also the closest PRC analogue to the EU AI Act's risk tiers and to lab safety-level schemes, but it is not equivalent to either: the EU tiers attach fixed legal obligations to a use case, whereas 分类分级 is a method handed down for sectors to localise. Word order varies (分类分级 / 分级分类) with no difference in meaning.

translations.notes: The canonical form. 分级分类 also appears with identical meaning, including within the same TC260 document.
